content: The A1C test evaluates the average blood glucose levels over the past two to three months by measuring the percentage of glycated hemoglobin in the blood. The Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) test determines blood glucose levels after a period of fasting, typically for at least eight hours. The 2-Hour Plasma Glucose (2-h PG) test, conducted during an Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT), measures blood glucose levels exactly two hours after the patient consumes a 75-gram glucose solution. Common symptoms associated with diabetes include excessive thirst, frequent urination, and unexplained weight loss.
